features: ⚠️ THIS VERSION ADDS NO DATABASE MIGRATIONS. It fixes the safety backup that runs before every update — the one that starts on its own from 1.11 onwards — which in five different places would not have done its job. It had never been exercised in the field: it had lain dormant for seventy-seven beta versions.

AN INTERRUPTED BACKUP PRODUCED AN ARCHIVE THAT COULD NOT BE PUT BACK — The backup advances in small steps, so it copes with slow servers. If a step was interrupted halfway, what it had already written stayed in the file but was not recorded, and the next step wrote the same piece a second time. The archive looked complete, with its size and its checksum, but could not be restored. It hit precisely the slow servers, the ones the small steps exist for.

THE RESTORE REFUSED ITS OWN SAFETY BACKUP — That backup is taken once the new version's files have already replaced the old ones but the database is still the previous one, and it labelled itself with the files' version instead of the version of the database it contained. So if the update went wrong and you put the previous files back — the most natural thing to do — the program refused its own backup, saying it came from a newer version. The archive now states the version of the database it holds.

AN ABANDONED BACKUP BLOCKED EVERYTHING FOR TWO HOURS — Closing the tab halfway through a backup was enough for the program to keep believing it was still running. For those two hours you could neither take another one nor restore: exactly what someone needs after watching an update fail. An abandoned backup is now recognised and closed, while one interrupted recently stays available to be resumed from where it got to.

THE AUTOMATIC BACKUP RETURNS FOR THOSE UPDATING FROM A PREVIEW VERSION — Anyone who had installed a 1.10 preview was not getting it, despite having everything needed: the check looked at the version number instead of looking at whether the infrastructure was there, and any number with «beta» in it counted as older than the final release. Anyone coming from a 1.9 is still correctly excluded, because that infrastructure does not exist there yet.

A FORGOTTEN FILE COULD BLOCK THE UPDATE FOREVER — Reported by an administrator who found «Download and Install» disabled with no explanation and every requirement met. The program was looking for a lock file in the server's temporary folder — a file it has never written: the leftover of a mechanism that was planned and never built. On shared hosting that folder is common to several sites, so any file with that name — anyone's, of any age — blocked everything without saying why.

IF AN UPDATE FAILS, THE PROGRAM NOW SAYS IN WHAT ORDER TO PUT IT RIGHT — It used to say only «you can restore the backup». Followed literally after a failed migration that advice fixes nothing, because the restore re-runs the same migrations and triggers the same failure. The order that works is: previous files first, then the database. That is now written down, with the reason. And it distinguishes the case where pressing again is enough from the case where it is not.
